spec.description: How often the indicators on it are read: equal periods of months (periodMonths from startMonth), equal periods of days (periodDays from startDate), or named periods listed by the month each ends (periods), one of the three (a kind rule; TAXONOMY.md D40, D68). The periods themselves are derived, never stored, and a reading is filed by the month its period ends, or the day on a cycle of days.

name.description: Deprecated: the name is metadata.name, as Kubernetes keeps it. Read from a manifest saved before 2.6.0 and folded into metadata.name; never written.

periodMonths.description: How long one period is, in months: monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly. A KPI read on this cycle has one reading per period (TAXONOMY.md D8).

periodDays.description: How long one period is, in days: daily, weekly or every two weeks, for an indicator read more often than monthly. An alternative to periodMonths and named periods; a reading on it is filed by the day its period ends (TAXONOMY.md D68).

startDate.description: The first day of one of the cycle's periods, so the rest line up with it: a weekly cycle from a Monday. Required with periodDays (a kind rule).

startMonth.description: The month the cycle's year starts in, 1 to 12, so periods line up with it (a financial year from April is 4). A period is named by the month it ends. Required with periodMonths (a kind rule).

periods.description: Named periods, for a cycle whose periods are not equal months: terms that repeat each year ({name, endMonth}), or survey waves dated once ({name, end}). All one form or all the other (a kind rule). Yearly periods are listed in the order the year runs, so the year starts the month after the last one ends; terms ending in December, April and July make a year from August. An alternative to periodMonths, which stays for regular cycles. See TAXONOMY.md D40.

name.description: What the period is called, such as Term I or Baseline wave. Unique in the cycle.

endMonth.description: For a period that repeats each year: the month it ends, 1 to 12.

end.description: For a period that happens once: the year and month it ends.

dueOffsetDays.description: How many days after a period ends its reading is due. The same for every period, equal or named.
